Subject: Marketplace listing: legal & SLA dependency matrix request

Hi Samira,

Thanks again for taking time this week. As we get the Acme Analytics listing preflight together, legal has asked for a clear dependency matrix that maps any marketplace "SLA" statements in the listing to the underlying Redwood commitments or fallbacks (hosted vs dedicated vs private). Specifically, they want a single sheet that shows:

- Where the listing copy references 24x7 support or uptime targets (exact phrasing)
- What Redwood product or contract term that maps to (hosted API, Dedicated reserved capacity, Private managed support)
- Any third-party dependency (AWS Marketplace entitlement, regional marketplace routing) and the responsible party for remediation
- Acceptable fallback language we can show in the listing if a hard SLA can't be guaranteed

Can you confirm whether AWS requires any specific phrasing for marketplace copy about support SLAs or third-party responsibilities? Also, if you have a template or required evidence bundle (e.g., SOC2 snapshot, signed SLA summary, support contact matrix) that would accelerate legal review, please share.

I copied Laura (legal ops) and Karthik (product) — if you need any artifacts from our side I can attach them. Goal is to have a complete matrix + evidence packet submitted to AWS by end of next week.

Thanks,
Marcus

Hi Marcus —

Thanks for the clear note. AWS Marketplace does not mandate that vendors promise a specific 24x7 uptime SLA in the listing itself; however, any claims about "24/7 support" or "99.9% uptime" must be backed by either:

1) A public-facing SLA or support policy linked from the listing, or
2) A vendor contract term (for private/dedicated deployments) with the reseller

For our side, the preflight team typically wants:
- A one-page dependency matrix (Excel) that maps listed claims to supporting docs
- Evidence files (SOC 2 Type II summary page, support escalation matrix PDF, customer-facing SLA doc if you have one)
- Trademark permission if you reference AWS product trademarks in copy (signed brand use PDF)

I attached the Marketplace preflight checklist (see inline stub: aws-marketplace-preflight-checklist.pdf). For Acme, please upload the dependency matrix and the SOC2 summary to the Drive link you noted; I'll escalate to our listing reviewers once received.

Quick clarify: when you say "fallback language" — do you mean fallback to "best-effort support" in region-specific scenarios? If so, include the exact sentence you'd like in the matrix and we can confirm if it will pass policy review.

Regards,
Samira Khan
AWS Marketplace — Listing Preflight

Marcus / Laura —

Received the matrix and the two fallback options, thanks. Quick notes:

- The conservative fallback will almost certainly pass, though it reads a bit customer-unfriendly; the marketplace team usually approves language that nudges customers toward Dedicated for guaranteed SLAs.
- The standard sentence is acceptable only if the matrix clearly ties the "24x7" claim to dedicated deployments and you attach the one-page SLA summary for Dedicated customers.
- We reviewed the trademark brief; the brand-use PDF needs a signed permissions form if you include explicit AWS product marks ("AWS", "Amazon S3" etc.) — there's a template in the preflight checklist.

Estimated internal review SLA: 3-5 business days after we get the completed matrix + evidence bundle in the Drive link. I'll open a ticket with the listing team today and update you if they request further edits.

Next steps I recommend for you:
1) Finalize the matrix with Karthik's notes and the dedicated SLA summary.
2) Sign the brand-use template if you plan to use AWS marks.
3) Upload everything to the drive link and post the HubSpot record ID in this thread so I can tie it to the listing ticket.

I'll keep you posted.

Best,
Samira
